title: Global patterns of ecologically unequal exchange: Implications for sustainability in the 21st century
status: Corrected R model executed — close fit agreement; exact replication unresolved

levels.mechanism: Investigates ecologically unequal exchange through asymmetries in embodied resource and labour flows between countries.
levels.strategy: Accounts for embodied materials, energy, land and labour in trade and examines relationships with income and other factors.
levels.technique: Eora multiregional input–output accounting, trade in value added and piecewise structural equation modelling.
levels.output: Embodied material, energy, land and labour flows; trade in value added and modelled statistical relationships.

title: Imperialist appropriation in the world economy: Drain from the global South through unequal exchange, 1990–2015
summary: Examines resource appropriation through unequal exchange in the world economy over 1990–2015.
status: Methodological profile under development; replication not attempted

levels.mechanism: Interprets net North–South appropriation of embodied resources and labour through unequal exchange.
levels.strategy: Reaggregates embodied-flow estimates into North–South net transfers and adds monetary valuation calculations.
levels.technique: Uses the Eora v.199.82 MRIO dataset reported by Dorninger et al. (2021), covering 1990–2015; adds monetary calculations.
levels.output: Net embodied transfers of materials, energy, land and labour, alongside monetary estimates.

title: How much growth is required to achieve good lives for all? Insights from needs-based analysis
summary: Synthesises needs-based poverty research and compares published decent-living energy and material requirements with current global resource use. It is not an unequal-exchange flow estimate.
status: Source-based methodological profile; independent replication not attempted

levels.mechanism: Examines how meeting basic needs and providing decent living standards relate to economic growth and resource requirements; does not estimate an unequal-exchange mechanism.
levels.strategy: Synthesises needs-based thresholds and published decent-living resource estimates and compares these with current resource use.
levels.technique: Literature-based synthesis and scenario comparison; adjusts IEA energy figures using a territorial-to-consumption-based ratio reported in Hickel et al. (2022). No full MRIO rerun.
levels.output: Needs-based income thresholds and comparisons of energy and material requirements with current resource use; not an estimate of unequal-exchange flows.

title: A Note on the Concept of Delinking
summary: Develops the concept of delinking through an illustrative comparison of national-popular and world-capitalist development strategies.
status: Source-based methodological profile in preparation; illustrative model not independently reproduced

levels.mechanism: Delinking reorganises development priorities around a nationally grounded and popular law of value rather than subordinating them to the world-capitalist law of value.
levels.strategy: Compares two illustrative development strategies for an initially identical economy over ten years, using shared assumptions about population growth, productivity and investment.
levels.technique: Illustrative comparative modelling of sectoral production, relative prices, income distribution and growth. Detailed technical derivations are referred to Amin (1982).
levels.output: Contrasting illustrative growth and distribution outcomes under national-popular and world-capitalist development strategies; not independently reproduced empirical estimates.
